note: Executable contract cases for the gated families. Each case is comparable and states exact method, origin and path, API version, headers split into static and credential-derived values, identity and read projections, a byte bound where the response matters, and the expected outcome. Every case also states which current Steed behaviour already passes and the smallest missing behaviour, so a case can fail because a shared capability is absent rather than because a recipe is wrong. A passing dispatch case proves Steed's behaviour against a documented shape; it never proves that a provider accepts a credential. No credential appears in this file.

kinds.parse: Build a recipe from the case and assert the interpreter accepts or refuses it.
kinds.dispatch: Install the generated recipe, connect one synthetic account and execute the case read through RecipeConnector with a synthetic transport serving the documented response.
kinds.transport: Drive the real RecipeHttp request gate directly, which refuses an unreviewed header or query before any socket work.
kinds.documented_bound: Record a documented engine or provider bound that cannot be executed locally, with the arithmetic that makes it a bound and the reason it is not executable.
kinds.gated_post_read: A documented read-only POST that no current contract expresses. The case records the official request and response shapes so a shared typed read-only POST contract can be promoted through real parser, review, adapter and transport tests once it is published.

cases.purpose: Notion documents Notion-Version as required on every request, so a read must be able to send it.
cases.currently_passes: Main now carries reviewed non-secret static headers, and the required Notion-Version header is one of the four supported names with a canonical date value, so a Notion identity request is now expressible.
cases.smallest_missing_behavior: None for this request. Writes and listing still need POST reads and identity-derived values.

cases.purpose: A database read projecting only fields present in the documented current-version response.
cases.currently_passes: Identity selection, path validation, pointer selection and result shaping all already pass for this documented shape; only the required header is missing.
cases.smallest_missing_behavior: The reviewed static header from notion_static_version_header.
cases.provider_acceptance: pending: an internal integration token is only documented by inference, and the projected fields are not yet confirmed against a real shared database.

cases.purpose: The documented user object marks name as oneOf string or null, so a bot with no name has no label.
cases.currently_passes: Main now carries reviewed identity label alternatives, so a documented null name falls back to a reviewed pointer instead of refusing the account or inventing a display string.
cases.smallest_missing_behavior: None. The fallback is reviewed in source and shown in the source review.

cases.purpose: A user-pinned numeric library id in reviewed source, with the item key as the caller destination.
cases.api_version: 3 (documented default; the version header is recommended, not required)
cases.currently_passes: Bearer auth, the pinned path segment, the documented item-key character set and every projected pointer already pass against this documented shape.
cases.smallest_missing_behavior: Nothing structural. One sign-in without a pinned library id still needs binding an identity-derived value into a later path.
cases.provider_acceptance: pending: no item schema is published, the documented identity route is written against the Zotero-API-Key header, and which data fields exist for every item type is unverified.

cases.purpose: A global id is not valid on the library item route, and Steed must not silently reinterpret it.

failure.documented: An invalid request such as an unknown item returns 404 Not Found. What a wrong id kind returns specifically is not documented.

cases.currently_passes: The request is dispatched with the caller's exact id, and Steed surfaces the service's answer instead of retrying with another id kind.
cases.smallest_missing_behavior: None. This is service behaviour, recorded so a failure is not mistaken for a Steed defect.

cases.purpose: A personal access token is documented as travelling in X-Figma-Token, not in Authorization.
cases.currently_passes: Nothing blocks a Figma identity read except the credential placement; the origin, path and pointers are already satisfied.
cases.smallest_missing_behavior: One reviewed credential-derived header value, carried without inventing a Bearer prefix and never in a path or query.

cases.purpose: The documented file metadata endpoint returns no document tree, so the read stays small.
cases.currently_passes: Identity, the two-segment pinned path shape with one caller destination, pointer selection and result shaping already pass against this documented shape.
cases.smallest_missing_behavior: The credential-derived header from figma_credential_token_header, or an OAuth token the user already holds.
cases.provider_acceptance: pending: whether a personal access token may call /v1/me is not documented, and the projected fields are not confirmed against a real file.

cases.purpose: Projecting metadata does not shrink the response: the document route always carries the tree, and the transport bounds the body.
cases.documented: The document attribute contains a Node of type DOCUMENT and is a non-optional field of the return value. depth is documented as a positive integer limiting traversal, and not setting it returns all nodes. No response-size limit is documented for any file endpoint.

engine_bound.behaviour: a response body over 128 KiB fails the request with an API error before any projection

expected.reason: A profile origin is one exact public HTTPS domain, so the real transport can never be pointed at a loopback fixture and its body bound cannot be exercised locally.

cases.currently_passes: Nothing: the requirement is a bounded document read, and the only documented levers are depth or ids, neither of which the transport can send.
cases.smallest_missing_behavior: A reviewed fixed query input for depth or ids, plus a live measurement of whether an ordinary file fits the transport bound.

cases.purpose: A successful HTTP 200 that exceeds the transport bound must still be a failure, never a partial read.
cases.currently_passes: The transport already refuses an oversized body, and this case exists so nobody relaxes that while adding a design subset.
cases.smallest_missing_behavior: None. This is a behaviour to preserve.

cases.purpose: Querying a data source is a POST read with an optional body, which no current read contract expresses.

documented_body_fields.sorts: optional array of property or timestamp sorts
documented_body_fields.filter: optional compound and/or group or property filter, maxItems 100
documented_body_fields.is_archived: optional boolean; archived pages are returned only when true

documented_failures.403: restricted_resource when the connection lacks the read capability
documented_failures.404: object_not_found or directory_not_found, including a database not shared with the connection

documented_limits: Supports paginating through up to 10,000 results per query.
A response may contain fewer results than page_size.
has_more becomes false and every page served from the capped result carries request_status.
documented_do_not: Do not parse, validate or store cursors beyond passing them back as start_cursor.
Do not send in_trash; it is not a supported query body parameter.
Do not assume any sort order when no sort parameters are given.
Do not poll this endpoint on a recurring schedule.

expected.reason: Reads are GET-only today, and a write is a single POST that requires an artifact, so a POST read can be expressed neither way.

cases.currently_passes: The origin, path, required static header and the cursor shape all fit existing capabilities; only the read method does not.
cases.smallest_missing_behavior: A typed read-only POST with bounded reviewed inputs, selected response fields and a bounded cursor, reviewed before dispatch like a write.

cases.purpose: Linear reads are GraphQL POSTs whose errors array can accompany HTTP 200.

reviewed_inputs.query: query Me { viewer { id name email } }

documented_body_fields.query: documented by example only; no body schema is published

documented_failures.400: Rate limiting is reported as HTTP 400 with the RATELIMITED code inside the errors array, so the status alone is not sufficient.
documented_failures.partial: GraphQL queries can partially succeed with HTTP 200, returning data while including errors for failed fields.

documented_limits: 2,500 requests per hour per user for an API key, 5,000 for an OAuth app, 600 per hour per IP unauthenticated.
A single query is limited to 10,000 complexity points, and the hourly complexity budget is 3,000,000 points.
documented_do_not: Always check for the errors array before assuming success.

expected.reason: A POST read is inexpressible, and an application-level errors array would also need an error contract that reports partial success honestly.

cases.currently_passes: Bearer auth and the origin fit existing capabilities; the read method, the body and the application-level error array do not.
cases.smallest_missing_behavior: A typed read-only POST with a reviewed query string, bounded inputs and a response projection that surfaces an errors array as a failure rather than as data.

cases.purpose: Dropbox reads are RPC POSTs whose argument and result live in the HTTP body.

documented_failures.401: AuthError with the error field in the body
documented_failures.429: RateLimitError with a retry-after header or retry_after field

documented_limits: limit is capped at 2000 entries and is approximate.
A list_folder or list_folder/continue call may return a RateLimitError when duplicate calls run simultaneously for the same user and app.
documented_do_not: Do not use email as an account key; use account_id.
Do not rely on email without checking email_verified.
Do not send app credentials to a route declared auth = user.
Do not use recursive listing on a huge tree.

expected.reason: Identity is a POST as well, so neither identity nor the folder read is expressible with GET-only reads.

cases.currently_passes: Bearer auth and the origin fit existing capabilities; the read method and the request-object body do not.
cases.smallest_missing_behavior: A typed read-only POST able to carry a bounded reviewed request object and a projected response, with typed error unions surfaced as failures.

gated_post_read_note: These cases stay gated on purpose: a read is never disguised as a create, arbitrary queries are not permitted, and no origin or header rule is bypassed. Nothing here ships as a profile.
